records.claim: One study on women undergoing fertility treatment found that those who had been treated with methotrexate for ectopic pregnancy (when a fertilized egg implants and grows outside the uterus) within the last 6 months had a lower number of eggs. Those who were treated with methotrexate longer than 6 months ago did not have a lower number of eggs. This suggests that any effect of methotrexate on the number of eggs might be temporary. Other studies have not shown a higher chance of problems with fertility (ability to get pregnant) with the use of methotrexate.
records.source_section: I take methotrexate. Can it make it harder for me to get pregnant?
